Definition: from G3326 and a form of G4862; betwixt (of place or person); (of time) as adjective, intervening, or (by implication) adjoining:--between, mean while, next.
BiblicalUsage: Peter slept between two soldiers the night before Herod would bring him out, and John's disciples asked Jesus to eat in the meanwhile. The word is the space between, whether two soldiers in a prison or the pause between one thing and the next.
TheologicalSignificance: I notice that God does His quietest work in the meanwhile: Peter asleep between soldiers, the church praying, and by morning the chains are off.
